chapter: Billie Holiday, Basie leadership and studio work
title: Why Basie got so many arrangers; writing for the band
summary: Arrangers came to Basie; those who wrote their own way and let the band play it succeeded.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Who was responsible for the idea of getting all this material from all these different arrangers, instead of like as so many bands do, just sticking to one or two?

You see, once you get a business going, where you have a machine that is turning out, people come to you; you don't go looking for them. When an arranger would come up and hear the Basie Band play and hear the Basie Band sound, then immediately dollar signs came in his eyes and he would say, 'Now, if I could just get these guys to play my thing, I will do it. I will write something for them.' But the main thing that happened that was wrong, guys tried to write like Basie played, which is the wrong way to do it.

You write like you write and then let the Basie Band play it the way the Basie Band played it and the way that I would rehearse them to have it played. Then they had the correct formula. But most of the guys never knew the formula, because they tried to write like Basie played. All of those fellas that were writing the Shillinger (PHONETIC) System and things of that sort were off on the wrong foot from the start and most of them never made it.

Most guys that had things played well by Basie just wrote things that they thought they would like to have played and then gave it to the Basie Band. We rehearsed it our way and played it our way and made it famous.
